choices.why: Correct in this family's unmutated case and wrong here: the deciding fact is present but nobody is recorded as having said it, which changes what a defensible response has to do. Recognising that is the whole test.

choices.text: Rely on it: it appears consistently in three separate notes, which is stronger than a single entry.
choices.why: The three notes are copies of each other, not three observations. Consistency between copies says nothing.

choices.text: Trace the fact to its originating author and note before relying on it, and mark it unverified until then.
choices.why: Correct: provenance is what makes a carried-forward fact usable, and repetition is not provenance.

choices.text: Send today with the imaging request attached and forward the report when it arrives.
choices.why: The service has said it needs the report. Sending an incomplete packet restarts the clock rather than advancing it.

records.goldBehavior: Do not treat repetition as corroboration. Trace the fact to its originating note and author before relying on it, state that it is currently unattributed, and either reattach its origin or mark it as unverified in anything you produce. Three copies of one unattributed claim are one unattributed claim.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: States that the fact is unattributed rather than treating it as established.
Recognises that repetition across notes is not independent corroboration.
Traces it to an origin, or carries it forward explicitly marked as unverified.

records.rationale: This variant applies PROVENANCE_STRIPPED — the deciding fact is present but nobody is recorded as having said it — so the response that is correct in the family's unmutated case is a trap here. That is the point of the family: the wording barely moves and the defensible action does. Competency targeted: Orders, referrals, and fax workflows. The gold behaviour is settled by the packet carried in this record — nothing outside it is asserted — which is why the acceptance criteria point at packet lines rather than at an external rule. The distractors are not filler: each one is a way a competent-sounding responder actually goes wrong on this material, and each carries its own explanation.

lines.text: 2026-09-01, walk-in at the front desk: the task opens as described — A referral for Lorelai Abubakar-Stern to Dr. Saoirse Mbeki-Lantz is queued to send today. Decide whether it goes. P. Kirchmayer begins it and records the routine details.
Insurance card image on file, captured 2026-09-01; no change since prior visit.
Preferred contact on file: walk-in at the front desk. Interpreter not required.
Later the same day, ownership moves to the incoming coordinator at shift change. The handoff note carries the task but not the reason it was opened.

Two days later, a returned message adds the fact that changes the answer: The receiving service's stated requirement for this scenario is that the referral include the imaging report it is based on. The packet contains the imaging request, not the report. It arrives in the original opener's inbox, who is now off rota for the week.
The packet was sent incomplete, rejected after eleven days, and re-queued from the start. The patient has meanwhile been told the item is in hand.

records.prompt: A referral for Lorelai Abubakar-Stern to Dr. Saoirse Mbeki-Lantz is queued to send today. Decide whether it goes. Work the encounter as it actually ran: the fact that settles it arrived two days late, in the inbox of someone who had already handed the task over, and the patient has been told it is in hand.

choices.text: Hold the send, obtain and attach the imaging report, and tell the patient what is outstanding and when they will hear.
choices.why: Correct in this family's unmutated case and wrong here: a multi-stage encounter where the deciding clue arrives after ownership has moved, which changes what a defensible response has to do. Recognising that is the whole test.

choices.text: Apply the new fact and update the record to the correct end state, without reciting the intermediate stages.
choices.why: The end state is right and the history is gone. Audit reconstruction is the point: the routing failure becomes invisible and repeats.

choices.text: Return the item to the original opener's inbox, since the deciding message went to them.
choices.why: They are off rota for the week. Routing to an unattended inbox is what already delayed this by two days.

choices.text: Reconstruct the stages, apply the late fact, name the current owner, and correct the patient's expectation.
choices.why: Correct: a late fact delivered to a former owner is a routing failure, and the audit trail has to show it.

records.goldBehavior: Reconstruct the encounter before acting. Establish in order what was known at each stage, who owned the task at each stage, and when the deciding fact arrived; state that it landed with someone no longer holding the task and was therefore never applied. Then correct the current position: apply the late fact, name the present owner, close the loop with the patient whose expectation is now wrong, and record the sequence so the gap is auditable. Do not present the outcome as though the information had been available from the start.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Separates what was known at each stage from what is known now.
Identifies that the deciding fact arrived after ownership moved, and to the wrong inbox.
Applies the late fact and names the current owner.
Closes the loop with the patient, whose expectation no longer matches the position.
Leaves an auditable sequence rather than a corrected end state with no history.
